The world's tallest Jain statue is located in the state of Maharashtra, India [d1][d4][d6][d8][d10]. Specifically, it is the Statue of Ahimsa — a 108-feet tall idol of Lord Rishabhdeva, the first Jain Tirthankar — situated atop the Mangi-Tungi mountain in the Nashik district of Maharashtra [d1][d8][d10]. This statue has entered the Guinness World Records as the world's tallest Jain statue, carved out of a single rock [d7][d8]. Prior to this, the 57-feet Gommateshwara statue of Lord Bahubali in Shravanabelagola, Karnataka, held the title of the world's tallest Jain statue until 2016 [d1][d5].
